# Artificial Civilization Laboratory (ACL)

> An agent-based simulation of hunter-gatherers in which nature is programmed and culture is not, built by Abdurashid Khudoyberdiev. No list of inventions, no reward for inventing, no language models. It tests whether culture and civilization can emerge from nature alone, and what stops them.

Key findings: about nine in ten useful inventions are never learned by anyone but their inventor; about a third of small worlds die out because too few people find a partner; teaching the missing part after a failed lesson raises transmission. Every study is planned and frozen before it runs; wrong predictions are kept.
